title: A sharing rule on an object without record sharing saves and silently does nothing
body:
domain:server#6 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CXCS98uhsFQYk64epE

Found by the #30209 card thread while measuring row 5 (os-dev-report 6665615192 on PR #30620, `out_of_scope_findings`, class (c) trap).

## What

An administrator can save a sharing rule (`sys_sharing_rule`) on an object that is not under record-sharing enforcement (measured: `sys_session`, `sys_account`, `sys_api_key`). The save answers `201`. The reconcile then logs `WARN SHARING_NOT_ENABLED` and writes no `sys_record_share`, so the rule's recipients see nothing more than before. Nothing tells the administrator: the rule sits in Setup looking active and never applies.

Measured: no widening. The rule grants nothing, so this is a misleading-configuration trap, not an access problem.

## Expected

The administrator learns at save time that the object does not use record sharing. Either the save door refuses a rule whose object is not under enforcement, with a sentence naming the object and how to enable sharing for it, or the rule is saved and carries a visible "not in effect" state. Refusal is the simpler contract; pick per the existing sharing-rule validation in `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing`.

Related: #30209 row 5 (the rule's object picker lists every object) is a separate decision on the same surface: option C there is this card's refusal.

## Surface

`packages/plugins/plugin-sharing` (the `sys_sharing_rule` save path / validation) and its tests; changeset per the outcome (a save refusal is a narrowing).
